{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Filter to completed orders only
df_completed = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Check for rows where revenue is exactly '999999.99'
qa_rows = df_completed[df_completed['revenue'] == '999999.99']

# Display these rows
print(qa_rows)

# Count them
print(f"Number of QA rows (revenue == '999999.99'): {len(qa_rows)}")

# Convert revenue to numeric, coercing errors to NaN
df_completed['revenue_numeric'] = pd.to_numeric(df_completed['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Check how many rows were parsed successfully
print(f"Number of rows with valid revenue after parsing: {df_completed['revenue_numeric'].notna().sum()}")

# Check if any QA rows were preserved
print(f"Number of QA rows with revenue_numeric == 999999.99: {df_completed[df_completed['revenue_numeric'] == 999999.99].shape[0]}")

# Confirm the actual number of rows in the cleaned dataset
print(f"Final number of completed orders with valid revenue: {df_completed['revenue_numeric'].notna().sum()}")

# Compute the mean revenue of completed orders
mean_revenue = df_completed['revenue_numeric'].mean()

# Print the result
mean_revenue"}
